thread:
elaine: Quick heads-up — saw steady GPU memory growth on long-context runs with INT8 KV cache. Start ~2.1GB, after 90m ~5.9GB on same model + traffic. Seeing occasional latency spikes (~200ms p99 -> 1.2s).

mike: Do you have jemalloc / GPU alloc traces? Could be fragmentation + host paging.

elaine: Pasted the short dump from the run:
```
KV_CACHE_METRICS {
  model: redwood-v2-7b
  quant: INT8
  runtime: 2026-03-16T21:03Z
  entries: 1_040_321
  kv_gpu_bytes: 6_301_824_000  # 6.3GB
  fragmentation_est: 18%
  pages_moved_to_host: 28
  host_paging_bytes: 420_000_000
  avg_eviction_latency_ms: 3.2
}
```

sam: hmm that fragmentation number is suspicious. Are we storing per-token metadata that isn't re-used?

nisha: Also: INT8 path uses the quantized kernel variant which currently disables some prefix compaction heuristics (kernel-selection -> falls back to generic GEMM for small seqs). That could increase allocations.

perf-bot: POST_PROFILING_SUMMARY:
- top alloc site: kv_cache::store_chunk (44%)
- heap-arena-fragments: 12
- cudaMemcpyHostToDevice stalls: spikes correlated with p99 latency

ryan: Repro steps I used:
```bash
# reproduce: long-context stress with batching mix of 1/4/16
python -m perf.stress_load --model redwood-v2-7b --quant int8 --context 32k --duration 90m --batching heuristic
# dump stats every 5m to /tmp/kv_dump.json
```

elaine: Important detail: batching heuristics changed last week — default now favors larger batches for throughput which increases simultaneous KV writes. Might exacerbate fragmentation.

mike: Two axes: (1) allocator/compaction (jemalloc tuning, periodic compaction pass), (2) eviction/paging policy (LRU -> size-aware LRFU + write-back batching).

nisha: Also quantization precision interacts: BF16/FP16 keep kernels that support in-place KV reuse, INT8 currently materializes dequantized tensors on the host for some ops. That materialization path is the noisy bit.

sam: Did we run eval with INT8 on our QA set? What's the perf vs quality tradeoff?

elaine: Quick eval numbers from last night (small eval set, same prompt mix):
- FP16: avg perplexity 12.4, rouge-l 64.2, latency baseline
- BF16: avg perplexity 12.5, rouge-l 64.1
- INT8 (current INT8 path): avg perplexity 13.2, rouge-l 62.8 -> ~1.3pt rouge drop, perplexity +6.5%
Memory: FP16 KV mem ~6.8GB, BF16 ~6.9GB, INT8 ~2.7GB (raw) but with fragment/host pages pushes effective GPU usage to ~6.3GB observed.

mike: So INT8 raw savings are big, but current implementation leaks/moves -> we lose those savings in practice. Also accuracy regression is non-trivial.

ryan: Possible short-term mitigations:
- force smaller batch footprint (decrease batching window) for INT8 routes
- add compaction pass every N requests to defrag KV arenas
- change eviction granularity from token->chunk to chunk->segment so fewer small allocations

nisha: Long-term: rewrite INT8 kernel path to avoid host-materialization, or add kernel selection rule: prefer FP16 kernels when fragmentation > X or host pages > Y.

sam: Can we add a canary that measures "effective GPU KV bytes" (gpu resident + pinned host pages) and flip to FP16 automatically?

elaine: Yep. Suggest gating that in the smart router: policy rules like `if quant==INT8 and gpu_kv_resident + pinned_host_pages > 0.7 * gpu_mem_limit -> route to fp16_variant`.

perf-bot: ACTIONS_CREATED: #4321 (investigate jemalloc arenas & compaction), #4322 (benchmark INT8 kernel rewrite), #4323 (canary route rule).

mike: For the jemalloc/arena thing, try MALLOC_CONF: "oversize_threshold:1,dirty_decay_ms:15000,muzzy_decay_ms:15000" on a canary and run 2h. Also enable `jeprof` to capture fragmentation.

nisha: I can take #4322. Plan: single-threaded kernel repro harness comparing INT8 inplace vs current path; measure dequant allocations and peak resident set.

elaine: I'll own #4321, will add metric for "kv_effective_gpu_bytes" and a short dashboard.

sam: One more note: batching heuristics + routing interplay — if we force smaller batches we pay latency cost but reduce simultaneous writes. We should simulate W-T tradeoff with our optimizer.

ryan: Agreed — I'll spin a perf matrix: batching_window x quantization x context_len and collect p99, peak_gpu_kv.

elaine: TL;DR: INT8 gives raw mem wins but our current path has host-materialization + fragmentation/paging that erodes benefits and causes p99 spikes and a measurable accuracy drop. Short-term: compaction + routing rules. Long-term: kernel rewrite to keep KV in-GPU for INT8.

mike: Nice. Can we get a summary slide for Monday eng-runtime sync? 2 bullets: reproduce + mitigations + ownerships.

elaine: On it. Will post draft slide and perf graphs tomorrow. :rocket:
